_meta.purpose: The 6-LEVEL AUTHORITY CASCADE. A module inherits its structure from the NEAREST previously-developed work; the search widens only when the nearer level has no SOLID answer. The corpus-wide average is the LAST resort, never the first. The ONLY thing that overrides a previously-developed module is the per-subject GLOBAL PARAMETERS (doc 14), within its scope.
_meta.authority_order: doc14 (within scope) > existing related module in the SAME SERIES + SAME TEMPLATE > same subject + same level + same template > same-template in-subject > whole subject > whole corpus. The nearer level always wins; a level with no SOLID pattern (ambiguous / 50-50 / fragmented) is OMITTED and the cascade CLIMBS A RUNG; ESCALATE only when no level confirms an authority and doc-14 is silent.
_meta.level_walk_note: The canonical walk-levels: (1) level 2 is series+TEMPLATE (the existing related module(s) in the same series that also share the template), not bare series; (2) there is no standalone bare-phase level (prefix+first-digit) — phase lives only inside subject+phase+template (year-level within the subject+template). Six levels total.
_meta.level_0_own_human_gold: ABOVE this whole cascade sits LEVEL 0: for a module that ALREADY has a human-developed build in 01-Finalized_Modules_, that human build IS the authoritative templated structure for the module — the conversion's target is to reproduce it element-for-element. GUARDRAIL: the converter DERIVES it from the raw Writers Template + Media List via general rules; it must NEVER read/copy the gold as an input. Level 0 is the comparison target, not an input — resolve()/PrecedenceResolver deliberately do NOT consult a module's own gold; they DERIVE (levels 1-6) and ADJUDICATE.
_meta.level_0_doc14_carve_out: THE ONE RECORDED EXCEPTION to Level 0: a doc-14 Subject Global Parameter whose family is MARKED overrides_gold:true in data/Subject_Global_Parameters.json is a FORWARD-LOOKING design-team directive that the gold library largely PREDATES. Within its scope, such a rule outranks the module's own human gold: conversions adhere to the doc-14 convention even where the gold does not, and a divergence from the gold that matches the marked rule is INTENTIONAL (verdict DOC-14 OVERRIDE) — never treated as a converter error, never 'fixed' back toward the gold. Full policy: Subject_Global_Parameters._meta.gold_override_policy (incl. its gate_policy and doc-14's own Mode-B sibling-structure note).
_meta.solidify_rule: THE STYLE-ANCHOR-REGISTRY PRINCIPLE: a CONSOLIDATION level asserts an authoritative value for an element ONLY when that value is SOLIDLY consistent in the group — a clear dominant pattern (its module-share >= solidify_share AND not a tie). When the group is ambiguous (a 50-50 split, or fragmented with no dominant value), the element is OMITTED at that level and the cascade DEFERS UP a rung (a coarser group has more data and usually solidifies). It never asserts a rule from a weak/ambiguous split. Encoded per level as decision:'solidify' + solidify_share + tie_defers_up.
_meta.reverts_to: the THREE-level adjudicate (doc14 -> sibling-band precedence -> corpus fallback). (Despite the '6' in the toggle name, it switches off the WHOLE cascade regardless of level count.)
_meta.consumed_by: app/js/PrecedenceResolver.js reads data/Module_Structure_Index.json (module_meta + modules) + this file. DATA OVER CODE: the level definitions, order, decision rule and reliability floors live here; the code just walks them. All groups are computed live from module_meta — no registry rebuild needed.

match_semantics.equals: the side whose full ancestor-ladder signature EQUALS the reference wins (levels 2-6, full granular_sig).
match_semantics.contains: the side whose signature CONTAINS the doc-14 token wins (level 1 gives a token e.g. 'col-md-8', not a full sig).

levels.describe: a per-subject GLOBAL PARAMETER (doc 14) that governs this element, within its stated scope. Overrides every level below.

the existing related module(s) in the SAME tight series (prefix + first two digits, e.g. BLL24) AND the SAME TEMPLATE-type, nearest-lower first. The module this one continues from. A single clear predecessor decides; a mixed nearest-window (no solid pattern) defers up.

ALL modules in the SAME SUBJECT (learning area, across its sibling prefixes) at the SAME year-LEVEL and the SAME TEMPLATE-type. Asserts a value only when it is SOLIDLY dominant here; an ambiguous split is omitted and defers up.
ALL modules of the same TEMPLATE-type (Standard/Inquiry/Fundamentals/Bilingual) in the same subject, any level. Solid dominant value only; else omit + defer up.
ALL modules in the same SUBJECT (learning area). Solid dominant value only; else omit + defer up.
ALL modules in the corpus. The last resort — a labelled fallback, never the primary authority. Solid dominant value only; if even the corpus is ambiguous, the cascade ESCALATES (no derivable rule).

engine_inherit._note: The LIVE engine application of the cascade (PrecedenceResolver.inheritMenu, called from ContentConverter on the overview menu). OFF by default (enabled:false), so default output is unchanged — the same pattern as the subject-parameters master_enabled:false switch. env INHERIT_ON force-enables (A/B), INHERIT_OFF force-reverts (outranks both). When ON, the overview menu's CURRICULUM column width is GENERATED from the nearest previously-developed sibling (resolveWidth(code, menu_curric_key)); on ESCALATE the default is kept + a cv2-note advisory is emitted. inheritMenu is layout-preserving (targets only the <h5>-carrying curriculum column; a col-md-12 band is preserved).
engine_inherit._note_effect: Keyed on menu|@h5, inheritance brings the overview curriculum column width closer to the human build; the menu sits in #header, so only the page skeleton changes. The JS and Python resolvers return identical results.
engine_inherit._roadmap: Enable one proven scope at a time. TWO refinements come BEFORE enabling: (1) menu_curric_key 'menu|@h5' is a per-page-AGGREGATE proxy — the overview curriculum column needs a page-context-scoped key so a lesson-menu h5 can't skew the width; (2) the ENG-family / banner curriculum width is baked in SkeletonBuilder's two_col_offset SHELL template (not the ContentConverter menu panes), so those families need the same gated consult at the SkeletonBuilder shell layer. The ContentConverter hook already reaches the pane-form (tab1Cols / flat-h5) menus.
